fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/tui/inboxapp with a fake runner: a row per inbox item in order, Enter on a row opens that item's action, an empty inbox shows one empty-state line; the tui-inbox-app testscript compares rhiza tui app inbox --once with rhiza inbox --json byte for byte.
fields.statement: The Inbox app lists what waits on the owner as one rexuikit List, a row per item with its kind, change set title and what it waits for; Enter picks the item, and --once prints what rhiza inbox --json prints.

fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/tui/inboxapp with a fake runner: submitting on a question calls session.message with the item's session and the typed text, on a blocker calls question.answer with the question, its change set and the typed text, then the app quits; Esc or an empty answer calls nothing.
fields.statement: Picking a question or a blocker opens a rexuikit Form with one TextArea; submitting sends the owner's typed words (session.message to the asking session for a run's question, question.answer for a blocker) and closes the app, and Esc closes it with nothing sent.

fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/tui/inboxapp with a fake runner: confirming on a signoff item calls run.approve with its run and the app quits; Esc calls nothing.
fields.statement: Picking a sign-off opens a rexuikit Dialog naming the run and what it waits for; confirming approves it through run.approve and closes the app, and Esc closes it with nothing approved.

fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/tui/inboxapp with a fake runner: retry calls run.resume and abandon calls run.abandon on the item's run, each then quitting the app; abandon without the Confirm and Esc call nothing; neither choice is offered on other kinds.
fields.statement: Picking a failed, gave-up or skipped run offers retry or abandon in a rexuikit Form (a Select, with a Confirm before abandoning); retry queues run.resume, abandon runs run.abandon, and the app closes after either.

Which inbox kinds does the Inbox app list and act on? The owner named answering a question or gate, signing off and retrying or abandoning a failed run: is a gate a blocker (a question blocking a change set), an accept item, or both, and are the other kinds (open, stalled, overlap, disk-low, usage-reserve, main-stale) listed read-only, left out, or given an action? Do the old app's other actions stay (open the item's Rex tab, take the advisor's recommendation, nudge a stalled session)?
Does signing off a run in the Inbox app only approve it, or can the owner also request changes there (inbox.request-changes, as the old app's c did)?
